about: Living map of what the app must keep doing. scripts/feature_guard.py verifies every anchor still exists and every forbidden pattern is still absent. Update this file in the same change that adds, moves or intentionally changes a feature.

features.name: Customer ledger, pending amount and receive payment
invariants: Ledger rows and the customer's pending amount are written ONLY through CustomerTransactionOfflineController (addBillTransaction / addPaymentTransaction / addReturnTransaction). Never also write the same event straight to Firestore (CustomerTransactionService.receivePayment / recordBillGenerated): that duplicated rows and doubled the balance.
Receive Payment is hidden when pending <= 0 and the amount can never exceed pending (button gate, sheet validator, save guard).
Every 'Bill Created' ledger row shows Bill Total / Received / Pending taken from the bill itself.
The duplicate-entry repair only matches rows with the legacy wording AND a same-amount original within 3 minutes.

features.name: Billing: create bill, received amount, service charges
invariants: Received amount can never exceed the bill total (field resets to total with an error, and save clamps again).
A bill is saved locally first (InventoryIntegrationService.processBill does FIFO stock + ledger-safe bill) and then synced; the customer ledger is written once, locally.
Other service charges are added on a full screen whose widget owns and disposes its own TextEditingControllers (a popup closure disposing them crashed the app).
Returns reduce the bill's pending/paid and post a return ledger entry.

features.name: Cross-device sync (Firestore <-> local database), low Firestore cost
invariants: main.dart initializeSyncServices(): SyncQueryHelper.beginSession first, all sync services initialize, LiveSyncService.start last.
Every incremental pull goes through SyncQueryHelper.fetchChanged (queries both Timestamp and ISO-string typed fields).
A newly synced collection needs ALL of: a firestore.rules match block, a sync service, an entry in LiveSyncService, and a registry entry here.
importFromServer must never overwrite rows that have unsynced local changes.
Sync services' initialize() cancels its previous timer/connectivity subscription before creating new ones and runs one initial sync.

NO background polling and NO Firestore listeners (every read is billed): sync services have no Timer.periodic, LiveSyncService has no snapshots() listeners, list pages must not open full-collection .snapshots() streams.
Push is immediate: a local Drift write triggers that entity's syncNow() after ~0.5s; failures retry after 2s, 5s, 15s and then every 30 seconds while anything is still pending.

Pull while a screen is open: screens that show synced data use LiveRefreshMixin (liveRefreshEntities) so LiveSyncService.watchScreen refreshes those entities every ~45s (foreground only) and when the screen opens. A new synced screen must add the mixin.

Switching a dashboard / web-shell tab pulls the latest data for that tab's collections (OptimizedDashboard _refreshTabData -> LiveSyncService.refreshNow, rate limited per collection). A new tab must be added to _tabEntities.
On resume / reconnect everything is re-synced and deletions made on other devices are reconciled (count() check).

forbidden.why: Firestore listeners cost reads; use watchScreen refresh

features.name: Firestore security rules for every synced collection
invariants: Each per-user collection the app reads or writes has a match block with owner + active-subscription access. Missing block = silent permission-denied and data that never syncs.
After editing rules the user must deploy them: firebase deploy --only firestore:rules.

features.name: Newest-first default ordering of lists
invariants: Customers, suppliers, companies and products default to Date (created) descending so a new record is on top; other sort chips still work and reset direction sensibly.
Equal sort keys fall back to name so the order is stable.
Expenses: newest expense date first, then most recently created.

features.name: Bill / quotation print formats (POS thermal vs Normal A4)
invariants: PdfBillService.resolvePdfFormat order: formatOverride, then quotation_type for quotations, then bill_type. Default 'pos'.

Plain bills and quotations must print exactly as before; new document kinds opt in through PrintBillData fields (formatOverride, documentTitle, numberLabelText, qrAmountOverride) instead of editing bill-only branches.
The payment QR amount for non-bill documents is qrAmountOverride (e.g. balance due).

features.name: Event / sales order invoice with POS or Normal format
invariants: Default format is 'normal' (the original A4 invoice) so existing users see no change until they pick POS.
POS maps the order onto PrintBillData (event charges, sub-events, items, discount, GST, advance paid, balance due) and renders with the billing POS receipt.
Totals in POS must equal the A4 invoice: event charges + sub-event charges + sum(item.total); balance = total - advance.
All share / print / preview entry points go through EventOrderPdfService.generateEventOrderPdf so they honour the setting.

features.name: Customer pending-amount report + send to the customer's WhatsApp chat
invariants: The report is READ-ONLY: it reads bills / event orders and takes the total from the customer card's ledger value. It never writes ledger entries or changes balances (no CustomerTransactionOfflineController in the report service).
The statement always adds up to the customer's pending total: open bills + open events + an 'Opening balance / adjustments' row for any difference.
The report icon only shows for customers with pending > 0; generating it must not change the existing Collect / Finance / Transactions / call / SMS / WhatsApp icons.

FilePreviewPage's existing WhatsApp/Share behaviour is unchanged unless whatsAppMessage is passed. WhatsApp (2.26) ignores the caption of a PDF shared from another app, so the reminder message is PRINTED INSIDE the PDF (buildPdf(message:)) and the single PDF attachment carries both. On Android: (1) tapping WhatsApp opens the customer's chat with the PDF attached (native share intent, jid + shortcut id, c_billing/whatsapp channel); (2) when the user returns to the preview within 15 minutes (or taps WhatsApp again) the chat opens via wa.me with the message typed in. Step 2 is optional because the PDF already contains the message. Do NOT launch the PDF share and the wa.me link together (startActivities): WhatsApp reorders them and shows its contact picker. Never block the user with a dialog on return. If WhatsApp cannot be opened the share sheet gets the PDF + message; web/desktop save the PDF and open wa.me with the message.
The Android FileProvider (billing_fileprovider) and the WhatsApp <queries> entries must stay, otherwise the direct chat silently falls back to the share sheet.

The report preview renders PDF pages at a low fixed dpi (renderDpi: 130). A 300 dpi A4 bitmap is ~35 MB and gets the app killed (black screen / restart) while the user is in WhatsApp. Other previews keep the adaptive default.
User text lives in all three localization files (customerPendingReport, customerReportFailed, customerPendingWhatsAppMessage, ...).

The report reads only this customer's open bills / events with one SQL query each (loadOpenBillsForCustomers / loadOpenEventOrdersForCustomers). The local database runs on the UI isolate, so loading every bill with its items per customer id made generation slow and time out.

MainActivity.shareableUri copies files outside the FileProvider folders into cache first. Dart's temp folder is the app's code_cache, which the provider cannot share; without the copy the direct chat share silently failed and the generic share sheet (Gmail/WhatsApp/...) appeared.

Hindi/Marathi message text inside the PDF is drawn with Flutter's text engine and embedded as an image: the pdf library cannot shape Devanagari (letters would be garbled) and its built-in fonts have no Rupee sign (English uses 'Rs.').

forbidden.why: report must never write the ledger
report must never change customer balances
full bills table scan per id made the report slow / time out
full event table scan per id made the report slow / time out
ClipData without the text makes WhatsApp drop the PDF caption (message missing)
launching the PDF share and the wa.me link together made WhatsApp show its contact picker

features.name: Quotations (create, list, print)
invariants: Quotation printing keeps isQuotation labels and uses quotation_type for POS/Normal.

features.name: Customer created-date range filter
invariants: The date filter is optional: with no range selected the customer list, summary cards, search and sort chips behave exactly as before (newest first by default).
The range is on the customer's creation date (createdAt), whole days, inclusive of both ends. Customers without a creation date are hidden only while a range is applied.
The list and the summary cards use the same customerCreatedInRange helper so the counts always match the list.
The filter is local-only (no Firestore query or listener) and works together with search and the sort chips.
Labels reuse selectDateRange / clear from the localization files (all three languages).

features.name: Sales figures after returns (dashboard, chart, invoices header)
invariants: A sale return never changes Bill.finalAmount; it raises returnedQuantity on the items. Every 'sales' figure (dashboard Total Sales card, Sales Analysis chart, Invoices header total) must therefore subtract the returned value, so Sales drops after a return.

The returned value uses SaleReturnMath (finalAmount / totalAmount ratio) - the SAME ratio InventoryIntegrationService.processReturn uses for the customer ledger refund - so dashboard, invoices and customer ledger agree, also for bills with exclusive tax / charges.
Dashboard Returns, Net Sales and profit cards keep their meaning; profit still uses the discount-only ratio.
Reporting only: these files never write the customer ledger or bills (ledger stays in CustomerTransactionOfflineController).

forbidden.why: gross sales ignore returns; the Sales card must show sales after returns

features.name: Splash screen branding (tagline, business badge, contact line)
invariants: The splash tagline is 'Power your Business' (all three languages) in flat solid pink #DD95D5 (_buildPinkTagline) with no shadow or 3D effect. It is display-only and must not change layout of the logo, title or footer.
The splash footer shows 'PREMIUM BUSINESS SOLUTIONS' and only the phone number (no location text).
The splash animations (logo, name, tagline fade) and the auto-navigation after startup are unchanged.

forbidden.why: location text was removed from the splash by request
the tagline is flat; the 3D extrusion was removed by request

features.name: Subscription / trial access gate (splash, login, dashboard entry)
invariants: A user with a paid or trial window that has not ended must NOT see the 'Subscription expired' screen because of a slow, failed or timed-out Firestore read.

isSubscriptionValid reads the server first, then the local cache; if neither answers it falls back to isWithinLastKnownWindow (the expiry this device last confirmed). Only a definitive answer (no user doc, or no valid trial/subscription, or window ended) locks the app.
The splash/login timeouts never deny access on their own: they use isWithinLastKnownWindow.
A missing signed-in user is only treated as logged out after Firebase Auth has restored its state (_resolveUserId).

forbidden.why: a timeout must not show the subscription screen to a valid user

features.name: Dashboard Quick Insights rows use the view-card style
invariants: Quick Insights rows (Top Products, Pending Payments, Low Stock Items, Upcoming Events) use the same raised white card as the view cards (_raisedGlass, like Stock & Payments). Only the icon tile and count badge carry colour.
Each row keeps its count, subtitle, chevron and tap action (_showQuickInsightDetail) on desktop (2x2) and mobile (stacked).
